Your brief: purple · Halloween · plug-in · not too cheap, not too pricey

Purple string lights, side by side

Five real sets of purple Halloween string lights in the mid-range sweet spot — roughly $20 to $36, all plug-in, all made for indoor/outdoor use, and all solid purple (no orange mixed in). One pick is marked; the rest are there so you can see exactly what the extra dollars buy.

Prices and specs pulled from the live listings on Tuesday, October 20, 2026. Prices can move — the listing is the final word.

The pick

LAMPHOME 66 ft Purple String Lights — 200 LED, 16 Modes

The most lighting effects for the least money here: 66 feet and 200 deep-violet LEDs for covering a porch rail, a tree, or a whole fence line, with 16 modes — the most of any set on this page — and you can link up to 8 sets end-to-end if the yard grows next year. At about 33¢ per lighted foot, it's the mid-range done right: not the $9 battery stuff that dies by Halloween night, and not a $40 splurge either.

Want maximum coverage instead? The ODEETRONIC below gives you 98 feet, 300 LEDs, and a slightly lower cost per foot for $9.30 more — the pick still wins on total price and its 16 modes.

How the pick was made

  • Pure purple only. Plenty of “Halloween” sets mix orange in — every set here glows solid purple, like you asked.
  • Plug-in, not batteries. Battery and solar sets dim fast and die mid-season; every set here plugs in and stays bright.
  • The $20–$36 band. Under ~$15 you're mostly getting short battery strings; over ~$40 you're paying for length you may not need.
  • Cost per lighted foot is the honest yardstick — it exposes the short “cheap” sets and the pricey pretty ones alike.

Before you hang them

  • Measure your run first — porch rail, roofline, tree wrap — then use the coverage box above so you don't end up 6 feet short.
  • Mind the lead wire. The unlit stretch from outlet to first bulb matters; the TW SHINE and LORRYTE include a generous 10 ft lead.
  • No timer? Add one. A simple outdoor outlet timer (usually under $10) makes any of these come on at dusk on their own.
  • Keep plugs dry-ish. These are rated for outdoor use, but a covered outlet or a weatherproof box keeps any plug-in set happier through Texas storms.
